newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower after weaker ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower after weaker ACCESS.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open lower Wednesday after a weaker ACCESS session and continuing cooler-than-normal weather across many parts of the U.S., market sources said.
September over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.34 to $2.355 after settling unchanged at $2.374 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, September last traded 2.4 cents lower at $2.35.
Early Wednesday cash prices at Henry Hub were talked at $2.34-2.36 as western heat continued to boost electricity prices in those markets.
Technically, September support was seen first at $2.30, and then at $2.20 and $2.15-2.16. Resistance was seen at the new contract high of $2.43.
In Tuesday's cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed eight cents to about $2.30. Midcon pipes were up about 10 cents to the mid-$2.20s, while New York city gate prices gained several cents to the low-$2.50s.
Separately, injection estimates for today's weekly AGA inventory report range from 64 bcf to 88 bcf. For the same week last year, stocks gained 84 bcf.
